operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table/column names (Customers, Customer_ID, First_Notification_of_Loss, Available_Policies) — must double-quote and preserve original spelling; case-insensitive lookup.
Composite PK on Customers_Policies (Customer_ID, Policy_ID) — sample_fresh_primary_keys must dedupe on the tuple, not single column.

Composite FK: First_Notification_of_Loss (Customer_ID, Policy_ID) -> Customers_Policies (Customer_ID, Policy_ID); pragma foreign_key_list reports two rows (id shared) — must be treated as one composite edge for consistency, not two independent draws.

Self-consistent FK chain: FNOL.Customer_ID/Policy_ID must come from the SAME Customers_Policies row; upstream draws each column independently from the parent column, so it will produce pairs that don't exist in the parent — insert succeeds (FKs off) but joins yield 0 rows.
DATE columns stored as TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD' (Date_Opened, Date_Closed, Effective_Date) — declared DATE dispatches to Date fuzzer; first element parses as int? no, so Date (not Number).

Effective_Date in Claims has values 1973-1992 while Settlements.Effective_Date is 1971-2009 and Customers_Policies dates are 2016-2018 — no cross-column date ordering constraint, but business ordering (opened<closed, claim<settlement) is violated by TS.
Settlements.Claim_ID is nullable (notnull=0) but FK to Claims; TS may emit NULLs there — fine for insert, breaks joins.
REAL Settlement_Amount: Number fuzzer with scale from 'real' (no args) -> scale 0, so ints in [-1,1] perturbed by ±1/±2 — implausible amounts (0,1,2,-1) vs original 1500-9800.
CHAR(15) policy_type_code: String fuzzer length=15, but original values are 17-19 chars ('Life Insurance') — length range from elements [min,max+1] will be ~17-20, ok, but fresh strings capped at 15.
VARCHAR(255) Customer_Phone: String fuzzer length=255 -> fresh strings up to 255 chars, wildly unlike phone formats; contamination adds random chars.
Tiny tables (4-15 rows): choose_table_sizes level-0 = 1+30*u gives 1-31 rows; Services (4 rows) may get 1 row, making Service_ID FK draws degenerate.
UNIQUE (Policy_ID) etc. declared inline on single-column PKs — redundant; drop_unique_duplicates will re-dedupe PK columns harmlessly.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on Date_Opened/Date_Closed/Effective_Date: template inferred from first parsable element = '%Y-%m-%d'; range = [min,max] of 5 sampled originals (e.g. 2016-2018 for Customers_Policies, 1971-2009 for Settlements) — fresh dates stay in that narrow window, so cross-table date comparisons (claim date vs settlement date) rarely match.

Number fuzzer on all *_ID columns: scale 0, range [-1,1] for fresh draws, but list range [min(el), 1] (upstream quirk: list_max overwritten to full max) — so fresh IDs cluster near 0/±1, not near original 100-4000 values; joins on IDs still work because FK columns copy parent values.
String fuzzer on Customer_name: fresh strings from charset a-zA-Z 0-9() length 0-40, contaminated 50% — names like 'aB3(x' vs 'America Jaskolski'; LIKE '%Jaskolski%' queries get 0 rows.
String fuzzer on Customer_Phone: fresh strings up to 255 chars, no phone structure — LIKE '%-%' or regex-ish patterns miss.

String fuzzer on policy_type_code: elements are 4 distinct values, p=0.2 fresh -> mostly reuses 'Life Insurance' etc.; ENUM-like queries (WHERE policy_type_code='Life Insurance') still hit, but COUNT DISTINCT may be 4-5.

Composite FK FNOL(Customer_ID,Policy_ID): upstream fills each column independently from Customers_Policies.Customer_ID and .Policy_ID — pairs (214,257) may not exist as a row; join FNOL-Customers_Policies returns fewer rows than FNOL count.

Settlements.Claim_ID nullable: Number sampler may emit NULL only if elements include None (they don't, null_rate 0) — so no NULLs; but fresh draws near 0 won't match Claims.Claim_ID (100-4000) -> join yields 0 rows often.
Settlement_Amount: Number scale 0 -> values in {-2,-1,0,1,2} mostly; SUM/AVG queries return tiny numbers vs original thousands — plausible-value FNs.
Tiny Services table (4 rows) with level-0 size 1-31: if size=1, Service_ID FK draws all the same value; DISTINCT Service_ID queries return 1.
PK dedup: sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate PK tuples — with Number fresh draws clustered near 0, many collisions -> tables shrink below requested size, sometimes to 1-2 rows.

No NOT NULL enforcement in Python: Customer_ID NOT NULL but Number sampler never emits None (no None elements), so ok; but if a parent is empty, FK fill gives NULLs -> insert fails on NOT NULL, rows skipped.
